0.11.1 is a patch of 0.11 and interoperates with 0.11.0: format epoch 7, backup format 5, protocol line `11` and every storage, wire and protocol format are unchanged, and the server, the gateway and `ursulactl` change only their version. 0.11.0 and 0.11.1 nodes run in one cluster, and 0.11.0 and 0.11.1 extensions work with either server and open, read and import the same streams. Upgrade a cluster in place with an ordinary rolling restart (`helm upgrade`), with no fresh install or data move. Upgrade the SQLite client by installing `@tonbo/sqlite-ursula` 0.11.1 or replacing the extension library. Rolling back to 0.11.0 is safe.

- **`open()`'s `token` takes a provider.** Pass an async function that returns `{ token, expiresAt }` and the package keeps the token fresh: it calls the provider before the first request when it holds no valid token, again after 70 to 80% of each token's lifetime, and at once after a `401`. Short-lived tokens no longer need a refresher process of their own. Plain strings and `URSULA_VFS_TOKEN_FILE` behave as before.
- **A token change resends a request a `401` blocked at once.** A request blocked `unauthorized` waited for the 30 s retry even after the token was fixed. Now `ursula_set_token`, an open with a new token or a change to `URSULA_VFS_TOKEN_FILE` sends it again at once, and a snapshot upload a `401` failed starts again at once instead of after up to five minutes.
- **Tonbo databases by name.** `@tonbo/sqlite-ursula/tonbo` opens a Tonbo database by name with an API key (`apiKey`, `TONBO_API_KEY` or the `tonbo login` file) and keeps its tokens fresh. `resolveDatabase` does the lookup alone and returns the stream URL and a token provider for any other opener. `@tonbo/sqlite-ursula/tonbo/pi` opens Pi Durable storage by name in one call, and `harness.close` closes it.
- **The README and error types match the shipped API.** `UnavailableKind` no longer lists `wrong_cluster`, and `status().replication.state` is typed as its six values. The package behaves as before.
- **Host directory records.** For hosts that snapshot or move a process or the VM it runs in: when `/var/lib/sqlite-ursula/host` exists, every owner open records its cache directory there before it claims anything, and fails with `local_setup` when it cannot. The directory is optional. Without it the extension writes nothing and behaves as in 0.11.0. A 0.11.0 extension records nothing.
- **`ursula-vfs-host inspect`.** A new binary of the extension's crate, built from `clients/sqlite-vfs`, reads every recorded cache directory and reports each root's unacknowledged commits and whether every root lock a live process holds belongs to a root it read, as one line of JSON. It never writes, locks or loads SQLite.
- **The write hold.** `ursula-vfs-host hold` takes the host directory's `hold` file and keeps it until its stdin closes. Meanwhile write transactions wait before they start, for at most 60 s, so the logs drain before the host freezes the workload, while reads, `synced()`, checkpoints and replication go on. The hold is advisory, and the inspection after the freeze decides. Without a `hold` file nothing waits.
- **A closed database reopens while a child process lives.** A root's lock was released only when its file closed, so a child process spawned or forked at that moment kept it and the next open failed with `in_use`. A close now unlocks the root first.
- **Logs are read in bounded memory.** The extension reads its local log record by record through one 64 KiB buffer instead of whole segments. Nothing else changes.

Known issues: the known issues of 0.11.0 are unchanged. Every change is listed in the [0.11.1 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#0111).
